history.summary: IDENTITY WEAKLY SOURCED - the only web record found for this temple is a MakeMyTrip listing, which describes it as an ISKCON-affiliated shrine on Hare Krishna Marg, off Raghunathpuri Lal Dwara Road, near Gopal Motor Garage, Yamunanagar. No temple website, news coverage, founding date, or independent confirmation found (treat as UNVERIFIED). The deity form is Radha-Krishna in the Gaudiya Vaishnav tradition ('Kunj Bihari' = Krishna of the Vrindavan groves). Do not confuse with the famous Banke Bihari temple of Vrindavan.

name: Shri Radha Kunj Bihari Temple
town_description: Yamunanagar is an industrial city in north-eastern Haryana, on the western bank of the Yamuna river, created as a district in 1989. It is known for its metal, plywood, paper and sugar industries and sits at the foothills of the Shivaliks near the Hathnikund barrage. The twin cities of Yamunanagar and Jagadhri form one urban agglomeration.
